quiz.q: How did the Jakarta Summit redefine the core purpose of NAM in the post-Cold War era?
options: It redefined NAM from simply avoiding superpower blocs to advancing the collective concerns of the developing world.
It transformed NAM into a formal military alliance to counter unilateral interventions by the remaining superpower.
It shifted NAM's primary focus toward creating a binding dispute-resolution mechanism for territorial conflicts among members.
It restricted NAM membership exclusively to democratic nations to address criticisms of being a club of dictators.
quiz.why: The Jakarta Summit affirmed that NAM is not just about avoiding superpower blocs, but addressing the shared developmental concerns of the global South.

quiz.q: Why does strategic analysis in Indian foreign policy favor prioritizing IBSA over BRICS?
options: IBSA possesses greater collective foreign exchange reserves and higher combined military strength than BRICS members.
IBSA unites three equal Southern democracies without the overarching hegemony and geopolitical friction seen in China-dominated BRICS.
BRICS strictly attaches developmental loan conditionalities, whereas IBSA provides structural adjustment programs for developing nations.
IBSA was designed to replace the Non-Aligned Movement as India's sole multilateral bridge to Western powers.
quiz.why: IBSA brings together three equal democracies with shared interests, whereas BRICS is heavily dominated by China and suffers from conflicting strategic objectives.

quiz.q: What distinguishes the IBSA Fund's operational approach from traditional Western development assistance?
options: It requires recipient nations to enact structural democratic reforms before accessing multilateral development funding.
It focuses entirely on large-scale infrastructure loans backed by sovereign guarantees from participating central banks.
It finances demand-driven, small-scale community projects with technical support and without imposing policy conditionalities.
It pools equal bilateral aid budgets that are disbursed exclusively through United Nations peacekeeping missions.
quiz.why: Unlike traditional institutions like the World Bank, the IBSA Fund finances demand-driven local projects without imposing policy conditionalities.

quiz.q: How does Prof. Rashid-ud-din Khan's view on NAM's post-Cold War relevance contrast with C. Raja Mohan's assessment?
options: Khan viewed NAM as an anti-Western military bloc, while Raja Mohan advocated expanding it globally.
Khan advocated replacing NAM with bilateral trade deals, whereas Raja Mohan wanted a permanent dispute body.
Khan urged subordinating NAM to BRICS, while Raja Mohan proposed merging NAM with the Commonwealth.
Khan saw NAM as a timeless platform for developing nations, whereas Raja Mohan viewed it as comatose.
quiz.why: Khan maintained that NAM remains a timeless platform for developing nations to address shared issues, while Raja Mohan argued it is in a coma and should have disbanded.
